Hence, in possible energy transitions on the Korean peninsula, partload efficiency improvements and smaller turbines are required in thermal power plants in order to ensure their effective participation in a future smart grid.

articleTitle: State Estimation of Distribution Network based on Historical Data Mining and APSO-BP algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: For the safety and stability of the distribution network, the distribution management system (DMS) requires high precision state estimation results as the basic information. If there are errors in line parameters, the precision of estimation results of Weighted Least Squares (WLS) state estimation method will be lower because the WLS model relies on line parameters. This paper presents a state estimation model based on historical data mining via multivariate linear regression. BP neural network is used to directly obtain the mapping between input and output, which would avoid the dependency on line parameters. Therefore, the proposed model would not be affected by the errors of parameters. At first, Recursive Least Squares (RLS) is used to establish a historical data model to calculate pseudo measurement. Then the pseudo measurement is taken as part of the inputs to BP neural network which is improved by Adaptive Particle Swarm Optimization algorithm (APSO-BP). Finally, the proposed method is simulated based on IEEE 33 nodes system. The results are evaluated through maximum absolute error and mean absolute error, which show that the proposed method has high precision and performances well in avoiding the influence of line parameters errors.

articleTitle: Control of DSTATCOM Using S-Transform
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Stockwell-transform (S-transform) based operation and control for a distribution static compensator (DSTATCOM) is presented in this paper for power quality (PQ) improvement at point of common coupling (PCC). S-transform which is a timefrequency analysis technique is applied here to decompose the nonlinear load current to extract the harmonic components. The main active power element of load current has been estimated from the extracted fundamental component. The deviation of the reference active component from the actual load current is used to control the insulated gate bipolar transistors (IGBTs) of the voltage source converter (VSC). The VSC currents are added with load current for PQ improvement on grid side. A model of a DSTATCOM based on it is simulated using Simulink and Simpower tool boxes of MATLAB with linear and nonlinear loads configurations. Satisfactorily performance obtained on a developed laboratory prototype of DSTATCOM validates the projected control algorithm. The performance is compared and found to be better than the Dual-tree complex transform based algorithm under varying load conditions.

articleTitle: Power Quality Disturbance Identification Using Improved Particle Swarm Optimizer and Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This paper proposes an approach for identification of power quality (PQ) disturbances based on improved particle swarm optimizer and support vector machine. In order to identify the PQ disturbances more rapidly and precisely, mathematical morphology (MM) which is an excellent analysis tool in processing the shape of waveforms with non-linear signals is used to filter out noise in the signals. To improve the classification accuracy of support vector machine (SVM), improved particle swarm optimizer (IPSO) is applied to optimize its parameters. Simulation studies have been conducted to test the performance of the proposed approach and the results compared with SVM, PSO-SVM and GA-SVM have demonstrated its validity.

articleTitle: Optimum Mode Operation and Implementation of Class E Resonant Inverter for Wireless Power Transfer Application
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This paper proposes the design of ZVS class E resonant inverter to be used in a wireless power transfer (WPT) system. Since the Class E inverter satisfies the zero voltage switching (ZVS) and zero derivative voltage switching (ZDS) condition, high conversion efficiency at high frequency can be achieved. All the components of the circuit are designed for optimum mode of operation and the inverter is made to operate at optimal switching conditions. The designed circuit is simulated in PSPICE environment and experimentally verified at a frequency of 333 kHz. The system is also tested for the WPT application and the transferred power is found out with different coupling coefficients.

articleTitle: Spatial Data-Based Techno-economic Evaluation of Solar Hydrogen Production in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) Region
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region is endowed with solar energy that can be harvested and stored as hydrogen, which has gained increasing focus as a secondary energy medium. This paper introduces modeling and feasibility analysis of cost-optimized hydrogen production, storage, shipment, and methanation in the MENA region. The analysis is based on the economic modeling of hydrogen production through the combination of photovoltaic solar power and electrolysis systems, utilizing NASA surface Meteorology and Solar Energy database (2010) [1]. A system of 100MW grid-connected photovoltaic PV power plant (grid-PV) in combination with hydrogen producing electrolyzer are simulated using spatial data for the MENA region. Then, the simulation assesses cost of methane production by Sabatier synthesis of carbon dioxide. The unit cost of hydrogen from a system, which consists of 100MW PV solar plant and electrolyzer, ranged 4-8 US$/kg. Methanation was found to be expensive vis-à-vis regionally traded natural gas. Location is a major determinant to hydrogen cost due to the difference in irradiation and logistics. In conclusion, this paper can serve as an atlas for mapping the cost of solar power and hydrogen production in the MENA region, and facilitates further research in the future.

articleTitle: The Input Displacement Power Factor Compensation of a Matrix Based Isolated Bidirectional AC-DC converter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This paper presents a control algorithm for input displacement power factor (DPF) compensation of a matrix based three phase isolated bidirectional AC-DC converter. The input LC filter of the converter draws signification proportion of capacitive current at lower loads and consequently, degrades the DPF resulting in overall reduced power conversion efficiency. The proposed control algorithm allows decoupled control of both output voltage and DPF and thus, provides a simple yet effective implementation for DPF compensation. The mathematical formulation of the proposed control is carried out. Subsequently, the effectiveness of control is demonstrated through digital simulation for a 400 V (RMS), 50 Hz to 48 V DC power converter operating from 0.5 C W to 2.5 kW output power.

articleTitle: Frequency-Constrained Unit Commitment Considering Battery Storage System and Forecast Error
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Security considerations such as ramp reserve and frequency limits are especially important in power system operation and control. However, with the increasing penetration of renewable energy such as wind power, the system frequency response in case of the power imbalance to become weaker. This paper presents a framework for unit commitment for power systems consisting of conventional generators and wind generators. The research framework also considers the role of battery storage system in maintaining the system frequency. Besides, wind power and demand uncertainties are taken into account with using forecast error modeling. The unit commitment is formulated as a Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) problem and is solved using CPLEX and MATPOWER.

articleTitle: Development of an Efficient Low-Cost Low-Voltage DC Microgrid with Power Array Conversion (PAC) for a Commercial Building Application
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: PV solar energy is becoming increasingly more prevalent in electricity generation for residential and commercial buildings. Since PV solar directly supplies DC power, a DC microgrid is an ideal platform for PV energy resource in building applications. Existing DC power converters typically have low efficiency of power conversion at light and heavy load conditions. Much research has been done on the efficiency improvement of DC converters, but material, technology and manufacturing processes all impose a limitation on efficiency gain. This paper addresses the efficient improvement of DC microgrid with a power array conversion (PAC) for a commercial building application. The PAC configuration utilizes an array with three equal and parallel converters instead of a single larger converter to cover a wide range of load conditions. As power conversion is a large part of power loss in DC microgrids, especially for step-up conversion, the proposed PAC is developed to improve the conversion efficiency. Analysis results show that the proposed DC microgrid can improve the conversion efficiency up to 6.8% over the existing centralized single converter configuration. The proposed DC microgrid with PAC also generates 2.91% more power than the centralized single converter method. A review of the converter hardware costs indicates that the PAC approach offers savings on the initial purchase of converter. Furthermore, an array with three converters can improve the system reliability since it offers a level of redundancy where one or two converters can continue to operate, albeit at a lower output capacity, when other converters are out of service.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis Of Parallel Inverter Based On Virtual Oscillator Control
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: In this paper, by improving the control strategy of virtual oscillator, a non-linear model for stability analysis is established, and a solution to the circulation problem in parallel system is proposed. The external equivalent of the virtual oscillator is the RLC resonant circuit. In this paper, through digital programming, the module is established with dual characteristics of controllable current source and controllable resistor, in which non-linear control is introduced. Through the phase-locked loop to feedback the phase change of the current and voltage in the line, it eliminates the circulating current brought by the parallel operation of the inverters. In this paper, Simulink simulation is used to control the parallel operation of two inverters with the same capacity and without interconnecting multiple lines. By conducting an experiment of voltage and current stability in the case of load-mutation, and conducting an experiment of circulating current suppression in the line with inductance is carried out to verify the feasibility of the system plan.

articleTitle: Analyzing an Agile Solution For Intelligent Distribution Grid Development: A Smart Grid Architecture Method
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The design of future electricity markets requires Distribution System Operators (DSOs) to emerge as an active player by implementing advanced technical solutions which improve their market responsiveness, process adaptability and meet their business needs. This paper presents a methodology that helps DSOs carry out such a complex task. The proposed methodology enhances the Smart Grid Architecture Model (SGAM) framework in the context of transactive energy and multi-agent system (MAS). The proposed method is referred to as agile methodology because it made the SGAM architectures Adaptive, Goal-oriented, Intelligent, Linked and Expandable (AGILE). It is implemented using an object-oriented application that facilitates the analysis of agility in the network management.

articleTitle: Cyber-Induced Risk Modeling for Microprocessor-Based Relays in Substations
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Once critical substations are compromised, attack agents can coordinate among their peers to plot for maximizing disruption using local control devices. For defenders, it is critical to enumerate and identify all digital relays to determine the systemic risks. Any combination of disruptive switching via the compromised relays can result in misoperation or immediate effect to the system. The resulting consequence of these attack's initial events would possibly incur cascading failure to a grid. This paper quantifies the criticality of substation protective relays with the combination of the outage level and its corresponding severity risk index. The proposed hypothesized outages are based on the type of protective relaying, bus configuration of a substation, and commonly implemented relaying schemes, such as bus differential, directional overcurrent and distance relays, are studied. This preliminary work also provides three approaches of determination in probabilities for sensitivity analysis. The proposed risk indices are evaluated using IEEE test systems.

articleTitle: Variable Wind, Dynamic Load, Constant Voltage Wind Turbine Generation System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The wind turbine generation (WTG) system is an emerging approach for distributed generation (DG) based electrical power. This is due to its freely available source, environmental friendliness and cost effective. However, the wind turbine based power is highly forecasting in nature due to environmental dependent factor. Hence, obtaining the reliable and efficient power from these sources is a challenge. In this work, a variable wind, dynamic load and constant speed wind turbine generation system is presented as one of the reliable power. The wind turbine speed is kept constant within a limit by varying a pitch angle even wind velocity varies and loads are dynamics. In this, the closed loop control of pitch angel is presented to maintain the constant voltage. The wind turbine generation system comprises a permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM) over other types of generator along with matrix converter to maintain the variable frequency to constant voltage, frequency power. The model of WTG is presented in Matlab/Simulink environment and its performance is studied through simulation results.

articleTitle: Automatic Generation of Input Data for Distribution System Simulation Programs
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Computers have become quite fast, and therefore, the most time-consuming process in distribution system simulations is, in fact, the preparation of input data cases for the simulation programs. Considering this fact, we have developed a computer system which automatically generates input data cases for various distribution system simulation programs from a distribution facility database owned by a utility company. The distribution system simulation programs include a voltage analysis program, an electromagnetic transient analysis program, a harmonics analysis program, a lightning outage risk assessment program and an earthquake and storm (typhoon) risk assessment program. The planning, operation and troubleshooting of a distribution system nowadays are highly dependent on these simulation programs. Using the developed system, a distribution engineer can automatically prepare a simulation data case by specifying a feeder, a transformer bank or an area to be analyzed, and then she/he is readily able to start the simulation. The developed system is also effective to avoid human errors in the data preparation process.

articleTitle: Multi-Day-Ahead PV Power Output for Improved Radial Basis Function Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) power output forecasting is a crucial issue in the PV power industry and power company. Nevertheless, the disadvantage of the existing PV power output forecasting models is that they often ignore weather fluctuation and uncertain information between the irradiation and ambient temperature caused by moving cloud, which leads to short of forecasting accuracy. This paper is to present an improved radial basis function neural network structure (RBFNN) with multi- parameters forecasting scheme to overcome above drawbacks. Result of the case study acquired by the proposed scheme is compared with two typical artificial neural network forecasting methods including radial basis function neural network (RBFNN) and back propagation neural network (BPNN). It demonstrations that the proposed model leads to better precision for forecasting PV power output.

articleTitle: Micro-Synchrophasors for Event Detection in an Electric Power System Simulator
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The complexity of the electric power system and its short-term variabilities prompt the need for high precision and high resolution monitoring of network states. Modern development of synchrophasor measurement devices have provided new perspectives for observing operation behavior and transient phenomena in distribution networks. This study uses microsynchrophasor measurement devices (uPMU) in a hardware-based electric power system simulator to simulate substation operation and power system events. We monitor PV current, perform fault studies and compare observability with a SCADA monitoring system. We find there is much potential for distribution network event detection and state estimation through synchronized measurement and high resolution monitoring.

articleTitle: Advanced Model Predictive Control Methods for Bidirectional Three-Phase Two-Level Converter for Solid State Transformers
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Solid state transformers involve three stages with the third stage being the three-phase two-level DC-AC converter. This paper investigates two different model predictive control-based methods of controlling this converter. The first one aims to reduce the average switching frequency to reduce switching losses. The second one is modulated model predictive control which can give fixed switching frequency. Both the proposed methods can realize bidirectional power flow. These two methods are compared using simulation studies in terms of active power delivered, average switching frequency, current THD and harmonic spectrum and the better one is then selected for solid state transformers application.

articleTitle: Fuel cost reduction effects by introducing storage batteries in a power system
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Renewable energy generation, such as photovoltaic and wind power, has been growing rapidly in recent years. However, as the penetration rate of renewable energy generation grows, the uncertainty and instability of power system increases. Therefore, it is necessary to find a way to contribute toward the massive introduction of renewable energy power generation. In the present study, the authors develop an interconnection-based unit commitment model by using mixed integer linear programming considering the function of batteries. The relationship among battery energy capacity, battery output power capacity, curtailment of renewable energy generation, and fuel cost of thermal units is analyzed using this model. As a result, it is found that increasing both output power capacity and battery capacity can reduce fuel cost and encourage the introduction of renewable energy resources. Furthermore, it was found that the rated output power capacity of the battery is more important than its energy capacity.

articleTitle: A Novel DC Line Fast Protection Scheme for the MTDC Grid
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Due to the topology of MMC base MTDC grid, the fault transient current has these characterisitcs of fast rise rate and high peak value after a DC side fault. In order to limit the fault current, the current-limiting reactors are generally installed at both ends of the DC line in the flexible DC grid, thus providing the boundary for DC line protection. The analysis shows the polarity characteristics of the reactor voltages between the faulted line and the normal line are different for a pole-to-ground fault. In case of a pole-to-pole fault, the reactor voltage characteristics between the faulted line and the normal line on the same DC bus are different. Therefore, identification criterion of pole-to-ground fault is constructed based on the polarity relation of voltage integral of current-limiting reactors. Identification criterion of pole-to-pole fault is proposed based on the ratio of voltage difference between the positive pole and negative pole current-limiting reactors on different lines of the same DC bus. Accordingly, the whole protection scheme is designed. Finally, a three-terminal symmetrical monopole DC grid model based on MMC is constructed, and the simulation results verify the validity of the proposed protection scheme.

articleTitle: Locally-determined Voltage Droop Control for Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Distributed energy resources have the potential to mitigate both undervoltage and overvoltage problems in distribution system through their reactive power capability. The most practical way to implement the voltage control is through a local droop control which requires no communication with the neigbouring buses or a centralised control centre. However, determining a suitable droop coefficient for the distributed energy sources at different locations in the system requires knowledge of the grid parameters. In this work, a practical way of determining the droop coefficients locally is proposed. The method is applied on most commonly used test systems, and validated against the traditional droop control. Results show that the proposed droop coefficient brought the voltage profile closer to the reference voltages for both overvoltage and undervoltage problems.

articleTitle: Reducing the Ageing of Transformer using Demand Responsive HVAC
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: With growing tendency towards larger buildings, aggregation at the building level has become a natural choice of energy management strategy. The distribution transformer is gradually moving into the purview of building managers. As a consequence transformer has its own role of playing as an agent in the energy management strategy. One of the major concern with the transformer is its ageing effect. Transformer ageing causes financial losses for the transformer asset owner,whereas utility will face the problem of operational losses. Temperature rise is the primary reason for ageing of transformer. Traditionally load shed is the option for high temperature rise in transformer. Since then the evolution of demand response concept in smart grids, it is used as one of the solution for peak load shaving. In this paper an algorithm is proposed for reducing the temperature rise in transformer using the demand response (DR) event. In this paper heating ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) load is considered as the flexible demand response (DR) load. HVAC load is controlled by temperature setting which is done using a smart thermostat. Temperature setting value of HVAC is decided based on temperature rise and indoor temperature. Proposed algorithm is simulated using MATLAB programming and the results are presented. Results show a reduction in temperature rise of transformer. The simulation is carried for 3 days and it is observed that the reduction in loss of life from 254 hrs to $48.6~\mathrm {h}\mathrm {r}\mathrm {s}$. These results explains the benefit of using demand responsive HVAC in increasing the life time of a transformer without load shedding which inherently improves the reliability of supply.

articleTitle: Research on Frequency Control of Virtual Synchronous Generator without Frequency Deviation in Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The Virtual Synchronous Generator (VSG) is viewed as an efficient approach to simulate traditional mechanical inertia of micro-sources inverters in microgrid. But the traditional frequency control of VSG cannot rectify the frequency deviation. This paper aims to reveal the reason of VSG frequency deviation by comparing different power-frequency control methods. Then the paper proposes a novel strategy directly inputting frequency deviation into the equation of rotor motion to get better performance of frequency control. Finally, a VSG grid-connected model with loads changing is used to test the characteristics of frequency response. The discussion and analysis of the results show the proposed frequency control strategy has good performance on secondary frequency regulation and system stability of microgrid.

articleTitle: Bifurcation and Lyapunov Exponent Analysis of Valley-Current-Mode SIDO-Buck Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Lyapunov exponent and bifurcation diagram are two effective methods to study stability of DC-DC converters. In this paper, the stability of single inductor dual outputs (SIDO) buck converter working in valley-current-mode (VCM) is studied. First, the operation principle, current borderline of the converter's inductor and the unified discrete-iterative model of the VCM SIDO-buck converter are presented. Based on that, the dynamic behaviors and Lyapunov exponent of this studied converter with variation of input voltage are emphatically studied based on the established discrete-iterative model. Furthermore, the stability criteria of input voltage are obtained. Finally, simulation result is presented to verify the theoretical analysis result on bifurcations.

articleTitle: Optimized Fuel Powered Induction Motor Drive For StandAlone Application and 40kw Load
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: For production of energy in remote locations and standalone applications the best resources may be the renewable energy sources like Photovoltaic (PV), Wind turbine system and Fuel cell. Fuel cell (FC) is the most environmental friendly device that uses hydrogen and oxygen to generate electricity without leading to pollution. The benefits of FC are almost zero pollutant emission and low noise emission. The development of powerful fuel stacks has increased the need to integrate them into power systems. In this paper we develop and study the behavior of a fuel cell fed 3 phase induction motor, simulated under different load conditions along with a 40kW load present in the system. A combination of fuel cells having a maximum power of 135kW has been connected to boost converter and three-phase inverter (with an inverter controller). Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) controller has been used to operate the fuel cell at maximum power point (MPP) by changing the operating voltage according to the load conditions. Fuzzy logic controller has been used in inverter voltage control to improve the efficiency of fuel cell. The behavior of a 5HP induction motor and a fuel cell system at different stages of operation has been discussed.

articleTitle: The Pattern Recognition of Residential Power Consumption Based on HMM
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The residential power consumption pattern includes user electricity activity and electric power utility, and the accurate identification of residential power consumption pattern is beneficial to the energy saving and management of power demand side. Based on the analysis of the user’s electric activity, this paper realizes the automatic classification of electric utility of home devices. Based on commercial office buildings, schools, hospitals, residential buildings and other places, through intelligent plugs, sensors, intelligent terminals, such as collection of information related to user activity data, this paper expounds the concept of power use pattern recognition analysis. The main process of power using pattern recognition is introduced, this paper discusses the different scenarios of power use the Hidden Markov Model (HMM) modeling method of pattern recognition, from single-user single-appliance, single-user multi-appliances, multi-users multi-appliances gradually in-depth analysis. Secondly, the main algorithms of learning and decoding are introduced, and the concept of association probability matrix is introduced. Finally, an example is given based on the actual scenario.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Optimal Method for Three Energy Entities in Integrated Community Energy System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: As the underlying terminal of multi-energy system, integrated community energy system (ICES) is featured with multi-energy complementary and integrated optimization operation. It is important to research on its optimal operation method for the development of integrated energy system and the consumption of renewable energy. Firstly, a model of ICES is established, including energy operator, user with distributed PV and EV charging agent. Secondly, a multi-objective optimal model is established, in which the three types of energy entities pursuit their own maximized interests rationally. Finally, the proposed model is solved in a typical winter scenario of the business ICES. Results demonstrate that the energy operator can get a certain profit by selling energy to the others. User with distributed photovoltaic (PV) participating in the profit competition is able to increase the utilization of PV resource and reduce the cost of energy using by selling its remaining PV resource. By choosing the bids of other entities and setting the best charging strategy, electric vehicle (EV) charging agent can not only reduce the cost of energy using, but also help users to consume the excessive PV power and reduce the peak load of distribution network in early peak hours.

articleTitle: Scenario Based Local AC Sparse False Data Injection Attack on Smart Grid
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Stealthy false data injection attack can evade the detection of state estimation and so put the smart grid in danger because the wrong states will affect the decision making in dispatch center. Therefore, it is crucial to study the impacts of cyber-attacks on smart grid and thus improve its security. Uased on the characteristic of false data injection attack, a power flow scenario based bi-level sparse cyber-attack model of AC grid with incomplete information is proposed in this paper. The proposed model is able to find the most vulnerable scenarios of the power grid. In this scenario, attackers are more likely to launch cyber-attacks, thereby this is crucial to the study of defense mechanisms against cyberattacks. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified on standard IEEE 30-bus system.

articleTitle: Hardware-in-Loop Validation of the Current Control Employed for a Fuel Cell-Supercapacitor DC System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The need for seamless inclusion and utilisation of clean energy for conventional energy applications are increasing on a day-to-day basis. This paper emphasizes the control design and hardware-in-loop implementation of the control for a low voltage DC system comprising of fuel and supercapacitor bank supplying an intermittent load. In order to facilitate controlled power flow among the system participants, DC-DC boost and bidirectional converters are interfaced to the fuel cell stack and supercapacitor bank. Current control strategy is employed to schedule and dispatch the interfacing converters in order to address the fuel starvation phenomenon associated with the fuel cell without compromising the unforeseen load requirements. Further, a special case of supercapacitor state-of-charge (SOC) protection is embedded into the dynamic control of the system to maximize the availability of supercapacitor. The performance of the dynamic control is validated for unforeseen R, R-L load variations using MATLAB modelling and analysis. In addition, Hardware Co-Simulation of the dynamic control is carried out on a Zynq ZC702 FPGA evaluation kit using MATLAB-Xilinx system generator (XSG) interface in order to evaluate the performance of the dynamic control in real-time.

articleTitle: Rapid Energy Consumption Assessment of Vehicle Concepts for Public Transport Systems without Detailed Deployment Data
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The energy consumption per passenger per kilometre and the total energy consumption of the system are two important criteria in the vehicle concept evaluation for a public transport system. However, the calculation of these two values mainly depends on the trip characteristics of the public transport system, including the trip length and the occupancy of vehicles, which are not readily available to public. The analysis of the massive trip data requires strong computational power and thus long processing time, which is not appropriate for the early phase design of vehicle concept. To calculate the energy consumption of a public transport system, this paper introduces a novel approach only based on variables that are generally open to public, including daily fleet mileage and the daily total ridership. This approach can be rapidly implemented for different vehicles and different public transport systems. Therefore, it can be used for a rapid evaluation of the vehicle concept designs for specific public transport systems. The approach is also useful for power grid planners to quickly decide if the infrastructure is ready for the electrification of the public transport system.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach Based on Process Identification for Estimating the Time of Arrival of Electromechanical Wave
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This paper describes the methodology of estimating the time of arrival which has been made viable by the convergence of the phenomenon of electromechanical wave propagation and the identification method for industrial system. First, the continuous time first-order plus time delay (FOPTD) model and the area-based method are explored, the proposed approach determines the time of arrival by taking advantage of this area-based method. Then, the available researches on electromechanical wave propagation is presented, which give the proper relationship between the time of arrival and the generator inertia constant. Next, a validation of suggested method for the FOPTD model is provided. And for the sake of solving the estimating problem that the time of arrival is in proportion to the square root of the generator inertia constant instead of itself, the novel approach is proposed. The comparison between the constant threshold method and the proposal will be carried out followed. Numerous simulations demonstrate the manner for estimating the time of arrival as having promising results.

articleTitle: An Automatic Pattern Recognition Methods for Power Network Fault Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The automatic pattern recognition of power network fault is important work for power network fault diagnosis in power system. This paper presents automatic pattern recognition methods based on wavelet packet time entropy and support vector machine (SVM) for distribution network operation states. The proposed methods employ wavelet packet time entropy to extract the most important features in the current when the faults happen in the power network. Then the type of power network fault is identified by SVM. The proposed method is found the most suitable pattern recognition tool in the power network fault diagnosis by simulations in typical distribution network. The simulation results show that the method has good performance on pattern recognition with low dimension of eigenvector, less training samples and high classification accuracy.

articleTitle: Coordinated Optimization of PTG and NGFP Considering Regulation in a Market Environment
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The development of multi-energy interconnection system has attracts intense attention recently due to its high efficient and environmental-friendly features. Power to Gas (PTG) technologies play an important role in the multi-energy interconnection system because of its energy storage and fast energy conversation abilities. This work explores PTG's revenue-obtaining possibilities in the market environment with daily fluctuations of both electricity price and nature gas price. The Coordinated operation with natural gas-fired plant (NGFP) and the participation in the regulation market is also considered to improve their overall profits. Finally, the simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed model and provide a viable scheme for the large-scale practical application of PTG technologies.

articleTitle: A Transformer Latent Fault Warning Strategy Based on Self-Adaptive Threshold Values
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Dissolved gas analysis(DGA) is considered as the most effective method to detect latent fault of transformers. But the stationary threshold values are tend to decrease the sensitivity of the fault early warning. In this paper, a transformer latent fault early warning strategy is proposed based on self-adaptive threshold values. First, upper bound and lower bound of historical gas concentration data is obtained by kernel - smoothing method. Then, the future threshold values could be obtained through a self-adaptive prediction model based on PSOGSA-kELM. Moreover, the warning strategy is made based on the comparison between new detected data and predicted threshold values. By the comparison between other existed warning methods, the feasibility of proposed warning strategy is testified.

articleTitle: Ground Resistance Measurement near a Ring Main Unit in Brunei Darussalam
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: A ring main unit (RMU) is used in the power distribution system to provide three-phase supply. This RMU needs proper grounding for reliable and smooth power supply to residential areas. In this paper, ground resistance of an RMU is measured using fall-of-potential method. The ground resistance is measured by Fluke 1625 Advanced earth tester equipment and the value is found to be 1.58 Ω. Soil resistivity is also measured near the RMU and calculated by CYME GRD software. The COMSOL Multiphysics software is used to simulate ground resistance, and the simulation results are found to be in good agreement while compared to the experimental results.

articleTitle: Relative Dynamic Performance Evaluation of Thermal Power Plants for Improving Load-frequency Control of Electric Power System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The impact of high penetration photovoltaic power generation system (PVS) on power balance has caused much concern. The increase in short-term fluctuation of residual load by intermittent PVS power output would require the modification of Load Frequency Control (LFC) in order to fully utilize the dynamic performance of conventional thermal power plants. The ramp rate is a good measure for the simplified evaluation of dynamic performance of power plant and is used to distribute the overall LFC signal to individual power plant. However, because the dynamic performance of thermal power plant is affected by various factors, the ramp rate would not be good enough for the detailed performance evaluation in terms of LFC. Therefore, the proper evaluation of dynamic performance of thermal power plant in terms of LFC is needed for reducing the frequency fluctuation. This study proposes adjustment coefficients for relative evaluating the LFC performance among power plants of different fuel types. Then, this paper demonstrates the improvement of LFC in a power system by using the proposed coefficients for distributing overall LFC signal to individual power plant.

articleTitle: Comment on “Distributed coordination of Electric Vehicles providing V2G regulation services” by E. L. Karfopoulos, K. A. Panourgias N., and D. Hatziargyriou
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This paper improves an existing adaptive droop based regulation dispatch algorithm proposed in “Distributed coordination of Electric Vehicles providing V2G regulation services” by [E. L. Karfopoulos, K. A. Panourgias N., and D. Hatziargyriou]. The paper proposes an innovative and effective framework for providing Vehicle-to-grid regulation services. However there are some small mistakes and weaknesses in the paper with respect to feedback signals for the controllers and the potential incapability of fulfilling charging demands of Electric Vehicles. Furthermore, the proposed framework can be improved by introducing hourly corrections and prediction intervals.

articleTitle: Application of a Varying Elements Tracing Method to Partial Refactorization in an Electromagnetic Transient Analysis Program
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Faster calculation methods are desired for electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulation programs, since circuits simulated are becoming increasingly larger and more complex. If there are time-varying and non-linear elements in the circuit to be solved, the solution process requires repeated factorization of the coefficient matrix of the circuit equations. The repeated factorization, which is often called refactorization, significantly increases the computation time. Up to now, the bottom right arranging (BRA) method has been applied for refactorization in EMT simulation programs in order to reduce the computation load. In this paper, the author proposes the use of the varying elements tracing (VET) method, which is one of the refactorization methods proposed for power flow calculations, for an offline EMT simulation program. Using some test circuits, the computation time by the BRA method and that by the VET method are examined, and the following facts are found. In most test circuits, both methods greatly improve refactorization speed, but in some test circuits, the BRA method shows degraded refactorization speed due to increased fill-ins. As for the entire EMT simulation time, the VET method improves the refactorization speed by a factor of 1.6 times at most. On the other hand, the BRA method improves the refactorization speed by a factor of 1.5 times in the best case but degrades it in some test circuits.

articleTitle: Voltage Lift Based Interleaved Flyback Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Conventional converters provide gain at the cost of high duty ratio operation, increased switch stress, increased control complexity and lossy power conversion. A non-isolated high gain DC-DC converter with two interleaved flyback stages is presented. The interleaved stage adopts a voltage lift capacitor to enhance the output voltage in the base stage of the converter. The secondary state consists of the secondary windings of the inductor in series to the output of the primary stage. This arrangement provides high gain without extreme duty ratio operation. The simulation results for a design of 100W, 24V/480V is presented which validate the feasibility of the proposed converter. This converter is a proposed to be used as a viable alternative in HID lamp and automobile applications. The hardware verification of the proposed converter is underway.

articleTitle: Fault Detection in an Islanded Inverter Based Microgrid Using Recurrence Plot Analysis
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Occurrence of various kinds of line faults (both symmetrical and unsymmetrical) at the point of common coupling (PCC) of a parallel connected inverter-based AC microgrid can affect the system transient behavior very badly. It is very much vital to detect these as early as possible to switch on the protection system in order to clear the fault. This paper is based on such a fault detection technique known as Recurrent Plot Analysis (RPA) of the load current for different line fault scenarios. By this method, the transients during different line faults at the PCC can be detected at a very infant stage. Also, different quantifiers related to RPA, namely, Recurrence Rate (RR), Maximum line (Lmax) and Determinism (DET) for the recurrence plot are calculated and compared for all kinds of line faults.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach for Onshore Wind Farm Energy Production Calculation with Different Topographic Heights
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: With the increase in the scale of onshore wind farms, wake effect is more and more significant in energy losses of wind farms. The siting selection of onshore wind farm usually takes topographical conditions into consideration, which generally include the topographic amplitude and the slope. However, the energy production estimation for onshore wind farm with different topographic amplitude considering wake effect would be complicated. In this paper, a new method for estimating the energy production of onshore wind farm with different topographic heights is proposed. The Jensen model is selected as the base and the wind shear effect is also taken into consideration to develop a stereoscopic wake model to calculate the energy production for different topographic amplitudes and slopes. The cases demonstrate that the proposed 3D model is suitable in estimating the wind energy. The framework can be adopted to wind turbines layout optimization for onshore wind farm with different topographic heights.

articleTitle: Unsynchronized fault location method based on the negative-sequence voltage magnitude for power cables of a simplified shipboard power system
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This paper presents an unsynchronized fault location method using the negative-sequence circuit for unbalanced short-circuit fault occurring in power lines. The magnitudes of voltages of both ends of faulty line are used to identify the fault location. Moreover, the fault impedance is not considered in to estimate the fault location, which means that this method is independent to the fault impedance.

articleTitle: Coordinated Offering Strategy of Thermal and Wind Energy with Flexible Ramp Products
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Conventional power and wind power suppliers may submit a coordinated offer to the day-ahead market. Such a decision depends on many uncertainties such as the forecasted day-ahead energy price, the real-time energy price, and the real-time wind output. Besides, many electricity markets have implemented flexible ramp products (FRPs) to enhance the system ramping capability during the real-time operation. Introducing FRPs may alter the behavior of the market participant. This paper proposes a coordinated offering model incorporating FRPs which is formulated as a two-stage stochastic programming problem. The simulation results demonstrate the impacts of FRPs on both the offering strategy and the real-time operation.

articleTitle: Active Perturbation Based Islanding Detection Scheme for Grid Connected Wind Energy System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Conventional islanding detection scheme based on Rate of Change of Frequency (ROCOF) has some limitations like non-detection zone (NDZ) near zero load-generation mismatch. Moreover, it may generate a trip signal even for non-islanding switching transients. In this paper, an active power perturbation i.e. a pulse signal has been introduced via Rotor Side Converter (RSC) of a Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG) based wind energy system to increase the rate at which system frequency drifts from its nominal value. Thus, the ROCOF relay achieves the set threshold even in its characteristic NDZ. Non-islanding transients are not affected by this perturbation due to the presence of grid.

articleTitle: Charging Demonstrator for Ancillary Service Provision in Smart Grids
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The target of this paper is to provide a charging infrastructure design for a carpark scenario which enables demand response (DR) management. The presented system not only allows an optimal charging scheduling to maximize the revenue for the carpark operator, but also enables the participation in DR. Numerous advantages to deploy a smart power sharing charging infrastructure in the future carparks have been discussed in the literature. A smart charging scheduling strategy leads to a better usage of grid power and improves the grid stability. Moreover it benefits the users to charge their own electric vehicle (EV) with lower cost and generates additional revenues for carpark operators. The utilization efficiency of the charging station will also be improved in the meantime.

articleTitle: Adaptive and Integrated PV Output control with Battery Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: An adaptive control system for battery integrated PV generation is designed to reduce the fluctuating in PV power production. The core component of the system is a four-layer power control system (PCS) for Battery Energy Storage (BES). BES responds to the power dispatch commands from PCS and charges/discharges to mitigate variations in PV power output. As a core part of the system, a novel PV power smoothing algorithm is proposed to reduce battery capacity requirements and reduce battery life losses by adaptively adjusting control parameter settings based on real-time system characteristics. Extensive simulation results based on real PV generation data have been presented to justify the effectiveness of the proposed approach and to show how several key parameters affect its performance.

articleTitle: An Approach for Discriminating Abnormalities In Compensated Power Transmission Circuit
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: In this paper, an intelligent fault diagnosis approach has been presented for compensated power transmission circuit (CPTC) system. The proposed approach is based on the application of signal processing and machine learning techniques. Discrete wavelet transform (DWT) has been applied on the 3-phase current transient signals for seizing the apt characteristics of the signal during different abnormality occurrences. The same signal features data has been utilized by ML model for the diagnosis of abnormalities in the CPTC system. Various test analysis (taking different possible abnormality in the system) has been performed in digital simulation for weighing the applicability and efficiency of proposed protection approach. The results of different cases have reaffirmed the application of proposed fault diagnosis approach for modern CPTC system.

articleTitle: A Primary Control Strategy for Power Sharing among Transformer Districts via AC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: With the growing penetration of Renewable Energy Sources (RESs) in the transformer district (TD), the power flow may not be consumed locally. Generally, the output of RESs and load power in a TD should all be measured to solve such issue. Also, the primary control for TD should not be too complicating to improve its expansibility in multiple TDs situation. In this paper, a primary control strategy for power sharing among TDs via AC-DC converter is proposed. The primary control strategy is proposed along with this new interconnection framework, trying to improve power sharing among RESs. Instead of measuring power of RESs and load, set value of shifting power in TD is calculated according to real-time power of related AC/DC converter and transformer, dynamically. This control fits single TD, and has good expansibility for multiple TDs case. Finally, the proposed framework and algorithm are validated through simulations.

articleTitle: Microgrid Management Encompassing AC & DC Renewable Generations with Energy Storages
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This paper presents a collated grid-tied microgrid system which employs cooperative energy management control in piloting energy storage deployments on a function of scheduled solar photovoltaic, wind turbine and demand load cohesively. The proposed management scheme seizes prudent power flow transactions that preserve the network’s performance and reliability through guiding state-of-charge switching algorithm. Conjointly, customary power-control converters are imposed to ensure mutual synchronization between respective generation units that tie to the distribution network. A detailed actualization of the proposed testbed system is constructed based on Singapore’s microgrid infrastructure in Pulau Ubin island using PSCAD/EMTDC simulation environment. Analytical and diversified case studies are inaugurated to venture its proficiency at systemizing all generation and storage assets in both islanded and grid-tied jurisdiction. The simulation results have exhibited practicability in utilizing the proposed energy management control system and its lucrative integration of renewable electrifications to alleviate much dependencies on the utility grid.

articleTitle: Individual Interaction Simulations of Integrated Energy Systems Based on Cobweb Theorem
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: As the growing energy demand and urgent need for higher energy efficiencies, Integrated Energy System (IES) has draw more and more attention. The optimization of operating strategy of IES is mainly in an integrated manner. In this paper, an IES model is established which composes of an electrical power system (EPS) and an elastic load center (LC) with mixed energy demand varying with energy prices. The two individuals operate independently objecting to maximize their own benefits and communicating with mutual information. In this way, the independent operation and information privacy are respected which is important in a real energy market. Cobweb theorem which is well known as an economic principle is applied to find the optimal operating strategy of IES. Simulation studies have been carried out in MATLAB and the results show that when the two individuals of the system pass over the other marginal prices and energy demands, the interaction can converge to the optimal operating point of the system, which is also the point of maximum social welfare. In addition, further sensitive analysis have been done on this model to find out the effects of pricing mechanism on system interaction results, the number of iterations, and the system turbulence. We also find that electricity price makes a greater difference to system convergence than thermal energy price.

articleTitle: Development of an Energy Management System Simulator for Analyzing Business Continuity Plan
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: In this paper, in a system that combines photovoltaic (PV) and storage battery (BT: battery), DC power bus (DC Bus) is controlled to a constant value for the purpose of supplying electric power to DC load and stable power supply to AC load. In the verification, 24-hour Energy Management System simulation using photovoltaic measurement value is performed on MATLAB/Semolina SimPowerSystems. Check the power of each part, the DC bus voltage and the remaining capacity of battery. As a result, the proposed simulator can maintain the DC bus voltage constant while satisfying the supply-demand balance. Weather patterns can be accommodated, and even if the load changes, the supply-demand balance can be maintained. It is confirmed that the downward trend of the remaining capacity is nearly the same for customers as well due to the weather. By maintaining the DC bus voltage constant, it is possible to construct a highly reliable system compared with the case where the DC bus is not kept constant, and even if it is operated as an independent system independent of the system, stable power without voltage fluctuation Supply becomes possible.

articleTitle: Optimal Sizing of Battery Energy Storage Characteristics in Radial Distribution Network based on Contrasting Investment and Net Present Values Approach
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This paper studies economic evaluation based on net present value (NPV) of the optimal sizing of battery energy storage (BES) to shave peak load in the radial distributed system. A study case in streetlights system is conducted as representing the radial system which drives peak load. Since there are various types of BES characteristics, while each type has different characteristics such as energy density, storage cost, and lifetime, the optimal BES configuration becomes complicated. Due to this complexity, to design a BES system to shave peak load, optimization algorithm, namely Crazy-PSO is utilized. The factors affecting the NPV and BES configuration are investigated such as BES lifetime, BES replacement cost due to run out of the lifetime, investment, saving cost, and quantity of BES configuration. Moreover, this paper's essence is to point out the contrast between BES optimization in investment and NPV objective functions.

articleTitle: Dynamic and Static Power Sharing Strategy for Paralleled Virtual Synchronous Generators in Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The accuracy of power sharing is one of the critical requirements to paralleled inverters in Microgrid. Due to the introduction of damping and inertia coefficients, the parameters matching method for power sharing of the virtual synchronous generators (VSGs) is more complex in the case of paralleled VSGs. Interactive effects of damping coefficients and inertia coefficients on dynamic performance of paralleled VSGs are not sufficiently studied. In this paper, the small signal model of active power control module is derived. Based on the model, the impacts of inertia and damping coefficients on VSGs transient state performance are analyzed in detail. According to the characteristics of paralleled VSGs, the parameter matching method for dynamic active power sharing is proposed in this paper. The effectiveness of the proposed active power sharing method is demonstrated by simulation results with the software Plecs.

articleTitle: Impact of Active Network Management Scheme in Fault Protection Design and Network Operation for Islanded Power System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The increased integration of Distributed Energy Resources (DER) and intelligent control technologies to distribution networks have succeeded in framing foundation for smart power grids. Design of protection systems and voltage regulation methodologies for an interactive smart grid will face new challenges with the introduction of new grid codes, active network management schemes and islanded operation. The active network management and optimal sizing of distributed sources shall change the operating point of the smart inverter-based DER in the islanded electric power system (EPS) continuously. This paper assesses the impact of such schemes on fault current magnitudes for various fault cases and voltage regulation at various nodes of an islanded EPS with distributed energy resources.

articleTitle: Non-Isolated Interleaved Flyback Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: There is an ever-increasing demand for viable, clean, energy sources. The main obstacle in using solar energy sources is that the output voltage obtained is too low for practical use. The obtained output voltage should be stepped up considerably in connection with the utility mains. DC-DC converters also find a place in smart grid systems with Distributed Generation (DG) units. The objective of this paper is to design an efficient, non isolated DC-DC converter. The proposed design consists of a two- phase interleaved boost converter with a flyback stage coupled to one of its phases. The primary features of the topology are continuous input current, moderate duty ration operation, and relatively reduced device stresses. Results of SPICE simulations prove the validity of the converter. Experimental verification of the proposed converter is to be taken up as future work.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of the Autonomous Decentralized Dispatching System of Generalized Demand Side Resources
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Taking full advantages of generalized demand side resources, such as controllable loads, distributed generations and so on, is of great significance in guaranteeing power demand-supply balance and improving electricity economic benefit. Conventional research focuses on optimization model and algorithms of demand response (DR). However, the scale of DR in practice may be so large and different nodes in the DR system may have different characteristics, which means users wm sign in or out at any time during the process of DR and even be fault and cannot response to DR signals. Aiming at these problems, this paper proposes and designs a novel DR system based on theory of Autonomous Decentralized System (ADS). Atomic nodes are divided and data field is constructed based on Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) protocol. Moreover, an autonomous decentralized hierarchical synergy algorithm for residential DR is also proposed which is very suitable for the ADS. In order to test performance of the proposed system, a simulation platform is established based on MATLAB/Simulink and 3 different conditions are simulated. The results show our system has good performances of online fault-tolerance, online scalability, which is suitable for large-scale DR.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Portable Grid
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This paper presents a design and implementation of a portable grid. A 80W prototype has been built in order to demonstrate the ideal that a standalone grid that utilizes solely on solar energy is feasible. With the right choice of equipment selection, the system could improve the lives of people living in rural areas or disaster-prone areas.

articleTitle: Microgrid fault detection methods: Reviews, issues and future trends
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Globally, microgrid (MG) technologies have become an important paradigm for integrating distributed resources (DR) into power systems. Growing cost, burdens associated with transmission and distribution infrastructure, and the environmental issues associated with combustion of fossil fuels, has attracted MG to provide electricity to various categories of customers. Despite the advantages, numerous challenges are still hindering the operation of MG working in harmony with conventional power system such as voltage and frequency control, optimization of distributed generation systems, islanding detection, power quality, etc. Another such technical challenge is MG fault detection, which must act in response to both the utility grid and the MG faults, for the proper functioning of the system. So, the idea of this paper is to provide a critical review of various fault detection techniques, and to categorize them based on the model based and data-driven based methods. It is also hoped that this work will provide some future directions for the researchers in discovering relevant references, and designing appropriate detection techniques.

articleTitle: Household electricity load forecasting using historical smart meter data with clustering and classification techniques
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The uptake of smart grid technologies and increasing deployment of smart meters have brought greater attention on the analysis of individual household electricity consumption. Within the smart grid framework, home and battery energy management systems are becoming important demand side management tools with various benefits to households, utilities and networks. Load forecasting is a vital component of these tools, as it can be used in optimizing the schedule of household appliances and energy operations. Inspired by the advancements in larger scale load forecasting, this paper proposes a novel forecast method for individual household electricity loads. Besides using smart meter data together with weather and temporal variables, which are commonly used in more conventional household load forecasting methods, this approach integrates the information contained in typical daily consumption profiles extracted by clustering and classification methods. In addition to the improvements in forecast performance, the method reveals key information about a household's habitual load profiles and other important variables which impact household consumption.

articleTitle: Fast Frequency Control Scheme through Adaptive Virtual Inertia Emulation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This paper presents a novel virtual inertia controller for converters in power systems with high share of renewable resources. By combining the analytical study of system dynamics and a Linear-Quadratic Regulator (LQR)-based optimization technique, the optimal state feedback gain is determined, adapting the emulated inertia constant according to the frequency disturbance in the system. The optimality is achieved through trade-off between the critical frequency limits and the required control effort, i.e. utilization of the internal energy storage. The proposed controller is integrated into a state-of-the-art converter control scheme and verified through EMT simulations. The results show a significant improvement in the frequency response compared to an open-loop system, while also preserving drastically more DC-side energy than a non-adaptive controller.

articleTitle: Security and Reliability Perspectives in Cyber-Physical Smart Grids
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Information and communication technologies (ICTs) are widely deployed in electric power systems to improve system monitoring, control, protection, and data processing capabilities. However, power systems' dependency on cyber infrastructure inevitably increases the risk of system degradation resulting from cyber-attacks. In addition, the intrinsic failures of cyber elements and the design defects of cyber-physical system architecture affect power system reliability. These two concerns are generally termed as “cyber-physical security” and “cyberphysical reliability”, respectively. While the two topics have received considerable research efforts in recent years, their distinctions still remain obscure among researchers. This paper succinctly summarizes the scopes, approaches, and major advancements in the two research areas with representative examples provided to clarify their distinctions. By revealing the inherent features of cyber-physical security and cyber-physical reliability in smart grids, this paper is written with the objective of facilitating future studies in these two areas.

articleTitle: Load Shedding Scheme with Deep Reinforcement Learning to Improve Short-term Voltage Stability
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: In this paper, a novel load shedding scheme against voltage instability with deep reinforcement learning (DRL). The convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are chosen to automatically learn the features and exploit the local spatial correlations from TS data of voltages. The DRL load shedding controller interacts with system dynamics through a sequence of observations, actions and rewards with two convolutional neural networks, namely critic and actor networks. The critic network is used to evaluate the quality of the load shedding actions and the actor network to determine the time, location and amounts of load shedding (LS). A global reward function is defined considering the recovery characteristics of voltages and total load shedding amounts to guarantee the coordination of under voltage load shedding (UVLS). The simulation is performed on the modified New England 39-bus system, and the results validate the voltage recovery performance and load shedding amount of the proposed scheme under different scenario.

articleTitle: Time of Use Price based Vehicle to Grid Scheduling of Electric Vehicle Aggregator for Improved Market Operations
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Large-scale adoption of Electric Vehicles EVs would increase average electricity consumption and peak demand of electrical grid. In addition, uncoordinated charging of EV would make situation more severe and require network reinforcement. One of the potential solutions to this problem is peak load management through EVs coordinated charging. In this regard, this paper put forward Time-of-Use (TOU) price based Vehicle-to-Grid V2G scheduling strategy of EV Aggregator (EVA) with the aim to optimize EVs coordinated charging and earn monetary benefits for all stakeholders such as EV owners and System Operator (So). For this, Price-based Demand Response Program (PBDRP) is proposed to enhance the value of EV owners. State-of-Charge (SOC), TOU-PBDR and modulation of charging/discharging rate is considered for the pragmatic formulation of V2G scheduling problem of EVA. Simulation result highlights the effectiveness of the proposed model regarding peak load management and monetary benefits for all stakeholders. Moreover, this model offers regulation services to SO for supporting grid stability and thus avoid inevitable contingencies.

articleTitle: Data Markets for Smart Grids: An Introduction
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Conventional power grids are being transformed into smart grids with the help of computer technologies. This has led to the generation of huge amount of data. Management of enormous amount of smart grid data poses significant challenge to the data owners. Currently, there are not much incentives available to encourage better data management among data owners. Generated smart grid data mostly stay with the owner of the data. Lack of a proper data exchange platform often prohibits the flow of data across various entities of smart grids. Exchange of data is necessary for efficient utilization of smart grid data. To address these issues, this paper proposes data markets for smart grids. The advantages of Smart Grid Data Market (SGDM) are outlined in this paper. Smart grid data and related services are the tradable commodities in the SGDMs. A market model is proposed for SGDM. Market structure, participants, commodities, attributes of data pricing, data licensing, data authenticity and other aspects of the proposed SGDMs are discussed.

articleTitle: Alternative Power-Based Pricing Schemes for Distribution Network Tariff of Small Customers
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The development of electricity distribution pricing is becoming an increasingly relevant topic due to various factors. The Distribution System Operators (DSO) face challenges regarding their tariffs of small customers when the customers invest in energy efficiency and small-scale energy production. Thus, the DSOs must evaluate their pricing practices to maintain a profitable and sustainable business. To respond to changes in the operational environment, transitioning toward power-based pricing is seen as a potential development direction. In this paper, we study various power-based distribution tariff (PBDT) structures and evaluate them from different viewpoints. To support the analysis, we provide a study where alternative tariff structures are analyzed based on data from two Finnish DSOs to investigate the impacts of the tariffs on the distribution fees of the customers and on the turnover of the DSO.

articleTitle: Development of Optimal Bidding Strategy for an Electric Vehicle Aggregator in a Real-Time Electricity Market
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: An electric vehicle aggregator (EVA) can participate strategically in an electricity market, on behalf of a large number of electric vehicle (EV) owners. Strategic bidding optimization and charging management for each EVA can benefit both the power system and EVA. In this work, a hierarchical optimization model for developing optimal bidding strategy and charging management in a real-time (RT) electricity market is proposed for each EVA to minimize its costs. The developed model is formulated as a two-level optimization problem in the framework of the well-established model predictive control (MPC). The first level optimization is to determine the optimal hourly RT bidding strategy of the EVA by a two-stage stochastic predictive optimization, with the charging scheduling of EVs formulated as a linear recourse problem. The second level optimization is to manage the RT charging of EVs in each time interval according to the cleared bidding quantity in the RT market, which can be formulated as a predictive linear programming problem. Both the first level and second level problems are optimized using the commercial solver Gurobi interfaced with Python language. Case studies demonstrate that the EVA can strategically participate in the RT electricity market and attain more benefits by utilizing the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Ensemble-based Randomized Classifier for Data-driven Fault Diagnosis of IGBT in Traction Converters
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Insulated gate bipolar transistor (IGBT) is one of the most common but fragile devices in induction motor drives. Fault diagnosis methods for IGBT are developed to increase the system reliability. This paper proposes a diagnosis method for IGBT open-circuit fault based on ensemble-based randomized data-driven method. A novel learning technology named random vector functional network (RVFL) is adopted to train and learn the historical IGBT fault dataset. An ensemble structure is designed to increase the diagnosis accuracy. Finally, time window is defined to illustrate the relationship between diagnostic accuracy and decision time. It is shown that more input information of the classifier, the higher diagnostic accuracy can be achieved, but with more time. By comparing other data-driven methods, the proposed ensemble-based method has a higher diagnostic accuracy within the same decision time.

articleTitle: Solutions for Remote Island Microgrids : Discussion and analysis of Indonesia’s remote island energy system
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Energy poverty is widespread in island countries, especially for the low-income countries. It is around 70% households in the Pacific island countries do not have access to electricity. With the fast development of renewable technologies, feasible and cost-efficient microgrid solutions are expected to mitigate this issue. This paper uses Indonesia as an example to investigate, develop and evaluate the potential microgrid solutions for the remote islands. There are six potential microgrid solutions are discussed, and two solutions (photovoltaic cells and storage; diesel generator, photovoltaic cells, and battery) are evaluated and identified as the most feasible, cheapest, and green solutions for the remote island microgrids.

articleTitle: Overview of Adaptive Protection System for Modern Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Conventional protection system has relays with fixed setting parameters. It becomes difficult to fulfill the protection requirements in variable operation conditions in general power systems. One of the solution to this problem is the adaptive protection which can vary its parameter settings or the operating characteristics in response to changes in the power system. Using such adaptive protection helps to improve the defects of traditional protection system which can make the protection system better: more reliable, sensitive and rapid. These characteristics and functions can be achieved by properly designing the electrical system and the protection scheme. At the same time ensure that the selected protection can detect and isolate all faulted portions of the electrical system. To guarantee the safety of the task of the power system, the protection equipment ought to be upgraded in like manner. Hence, the energetic structure of power system and their different working conditions need the advancement of adaptive protection techniques. This paper provides the concepts for the general and modern power system protections and highlights the adaptive protection scheme. The overall structure of the adaptive protection is described. The recommendations including software and functions for the future power systems are discussed.

articleTitle: A Numerical Protection Strategy for Medium-Voltage Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
